summary:
TERRA-SHIELD is an SI-assisted landslide visualization and experimental hazard forecasting platform built for NASA Space Apps' Dancing with the SARs challenge. It makes complex terrain and satellite observations easier to explore through an interactive 3D map with color-coded landslide hazard estimates.
Our Terra In House Model combines XGBoost machine learning with physics-based slope stability calculations and environmental inputs such as rainfall, soil properties, and elevation. Users can inspect uncertainty, estimated stability, potential runout paths, and weather-driven projections up to 72 hours. The platform also displays available NASA–ISRO NISAR L-band radar observations, including coherence and polarimetric data, with their coverage and acquisition details. These observations provide additional context rather than directly training the current hazard model.
Because the in-house model is experimental and not globally validated, NASA LHASA is included for independent comparison. An SI-assisted copilot helps users navigate and interpret results. By bringing SAR evidence, terrain analysis, and model comparisons into one accessible workspace, TERRA-SHIELD supports landslide research and hazard awareness without claiming operational early-warning accuracy.
details:
TERRA-SHIELD

SI-Assisted Landslide Visualization and Experimental Hazard Forecasting

Team Orangeo | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 | Dancing with the SARs

1. Project Overview

TERRA-SHIELD is an interactive landslide visualization and experimental forecasting platform designed to make satellite observations, terrain characteristics, and hazard assessments more accessible. It integrates environmental data, satellite radar evidence, and scientific models into a unified geospatial workspace.

2. Functionality and Visualization

Users can search locations, enter coordinates, or select terrain on a global 3D map. The platform displays color-coded H3 hexagonal grids representing experimental landslide hazard estimates.

Individual cells provide slope characteristics, factor-of-safety estimates, uncertainty intervals, and conditional landslide runout corridors. Weather-driven projections are available for 24, 48, and 72 hours when sufficient forecast data exists.

3. Terra In House Model

Our primary prediction approach combines XGBoost machine learning with physics-based slope stability calculations. It incorporates 25 environmental, mechanical, and interaction features.

The physical engine applies infinite-slope stability equations, transient rainfall infiltration principles, and First-Order Second-Moment (FOSM) uncertainty propagation.

Environmental sources include Open-Meteo, AWS Terrarium elevation data, ISRIC SoilGrids, NASA POWER, USGS earthquake information, and GloFAS river-discharge estimates. NASA COOLR historical landslide records contributed to model development.

4. NASA–ISRO NISAR Integration

Addressing the Dancing with the SARs challenge, TERRA-SHIELD integrates NASA–ISRO NISAR L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar observations.

The system supports satellite acquisition discovery and authenticated extraction of GUNW coherence and GCOV polarimetric HH/HV measurements through NASA Harmony.

Available measurements are displayed alongside terrain analysis, retaining acquisition dates, spatial coverage, and source provenance.

NISAR currently provides observational context rather than directly trained features for the in-house classifier.

5. NASA LHASA Comparison

Recognizing limitations involving uncertain soil properties, incomplete observations, and restricted training evidence, NASA LHASA is integrated as an independent comparison.

Users can inspect NASA's Today and Tomorrow hazard products alongside Terra's experimental estimates. A rainfall-only baseline provides additional diagnostic context. Differences in resolution and interpretation are preserved.

6. SI-Assisted Interaction and Development

An SI-assisted copilot supports location searches, terrain inspection, model switching, and evidence-grounded explanations. Deterministic map commands operate without external credentials, while generated explanations require a user-configured provider.

The platform uses Python, TypeScript, React, FastAPI, XGBoost, Scikit-learn, MapLibre GL, and H3, with Docker and Railway supporting deployment.

7. Innovation and Intended Impact

TERRA-SHIELD combines satellite radar observations, physical slope mechanics, machine learning, and interactive visualization within a single accessible platform.

Our team prioritized scientific transparency, data provenance, uncertainty reporting, accessibility, and computational efficiency.

The project aims to support landslide research, environmental awareness, and future disaster-preparedness applications. Predictions remain experimental and require independent validation before operational warning use.
